claims.text: For \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\), \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and this submodule is an ideal. [source-2@L1310-L1321|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1310: In order both to suppress the variable set $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ from the
1311: notation and to make more convenient use of symmetric function
1312: identities, we will work within a quotient of the {\it ring of
1313:   symmetric functions} with integral coefficients
1314: $$
1315: \Lambda=\Lambda_\ZZ(x_1,x_2,\ldots);
1316: $$
1317: see \cite[Chapter 1]{Macdonald-symm-fns}, \cite[Chapter 7]{Stanley-EC2}.
1318: The $\ZZ$-basis for $\Lambda$ given by the Schur functions $s_\lambda$ 
1319: has the property that the $\ZZ$-submodule $I_{r,n-r}$ spanned by all $s_\lambda$
1320: with  $\lambda \not\subseteq (n-r)^r$ forms an ideal, and the
1321: map sending $s_\lambda$ to $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ induces an isomorphism

claims.text: The map \(s_\lambda\mapsto s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\) induces \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J}/\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^W_+\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J}\), and the surviving Schur classes are indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\). [source-2@L1321-L1331|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1321: map sending $s_\lambda$ to $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ induces an isomorphism
1322: $$
1323: \Lambda/I_{r,n-r} \quad \overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow} \quad \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J}/\ZZ[\xx]^W_+ \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J} 
1324:                      \quad \left( \cong H^\star(G/P_J,\ZZ) \right) 
1325: $$
1326: Thus $H^\star(G/P_J,\ZZ)$ has $\ZZ$-basis given by 
1327: $$
1328: \{ \sigma_w: w \in W^J \}
1329: %  =   \{ \schubp_w: w \in W \text{ is }r-\text{grassmannian} \}
1330:   = \{s_\lambda: \lambda \subseteq (n-r)^r \}.
1331: $$

claims.text: Writing \(q=n-r\), the excerpt yields \[ I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\not\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda,\qquad \Lambda/I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda. \] The second equality follows by quotienting the Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis by the coordinate submodule defining \(I_{r,q}\).
